title: The combat of Jataayu and Ravana
introduction: The combat of Jataayu and Ravana ensues now, as Ravana was adamantine to the righteous sermons of Jataayu. In combating with Ravana, Jataayu shatters Ravana's bows, arrows, and chariot and kills the mules of the chariot and plucks off the head of the charioteer with his beak. Further Jataayu attacks on the body of Ravana lacerating severally. Enraged at the bird-hits Ravana severs that eagle's wings, feet, and sides. Then seeing that fallen eagle Seetha weeps over, as if Jataayu is her own relative.
closing: The character of Jataayu is not introduced just to give information to Rama at the time of his physical death. He is an example of self-duteous, self-dedicated, unpaid servant to his master. In Ch.14 of this Aranya canto when Jataayu firstly met Rama he says: so aham vāsa sahāyaḥ te bhaviṣyāmi yadi icchasi | idam durgam hi kāntāram mṛga rākṣasa sevitam sītām ca tāta rakṣiṣye tvayi yāte salakṣmaṇe ||"That is what I am, I will be your helpmate at your residence, should you wish so, for this forest is one that is impassable and adorned by predators and demons...oh boy, I wish to protect Seetha, if you go out of your residence with Lakshmana..." 3-14-34 And Jataayu kept up his pledge in 'helping Rama and protecting Seetha' as much as he can, without hesitation. This selfless service and sermons he rendered to Ravana are exemplary. This is called dāsya bhakti 'devoutness through selfless service...' and service whether paid or unpaid is thus to be rendered selflessly - is the lesson he taught.

Secondly, birds hitting airplanes is not a recent phenomenon and it existed even before airplanes were invented, as is evident from Jataayu's hitting Ravana's aircraft. And Ravana's aircraft that is variously and amazingly portrayed by the sage-poet, is nothing before a bird. Hence, Ravana should have used some other latest state of art technology to prevent such bird-hits. This is to say, any artificial paraphernalia is nothing before a living organism, and Hanuma, a mere monkey, taking lessons from Jataayu, a mere eagle, reduces even the artificially devised Lanka to ashes.
इति वाल्मीकि रामायणे आदि काव्ये अरण्य काण्डे एक पंचाशः सर्गः
Thus, this is the 51st chapter in Aranya Kanda of Valmiki Ramayana, the First Epic poem of India.

verses.devanagari:
इति उक्तः क्रोध ताम्राक्षः तप्त कांचन कुण्डलः |
राक्षसेन्द्रो अभिदुद्राव पतगेन्द्रम् अमर्षणः
verses.iast:
iti uktaḥ krodha tāmrākśaḥ tapta kāṃcana kuṇḍalaḥ |
rākśasendro abhidudrāva patagendram amarṣaṇaḥ
verses.translation: When Ravana is spoken to by Jataayu with judicious words, Ravana's eyes reddened infuriately, and his burnished golden ear-knobs flickered injuriously, and that lord of demons dashed towards the lord of birds, intolerantly.
notes: Ravana's ear-knobs jerked flickeringly, as if they are fireballsas, when he gnashed his teeth in anger. Here another type of rendering for this verse is available in other versions, which reads: iti uktasya yathā nyāyam rāvaṇasya jaṭāyuṣā | kruddhasya agni nibhāḥ sarvā rejuḥ vimśati dṛṣṭayaḥ ||'thus when Jataayu spoke to Ravana in judicious words, all the twenty eyes of infuriated Ravana are torched, like torchlit fires...'

verses.devanagari:
स संप्रहारः तुमुलः तयोः तस्मिन् महा मृधे |
बभूव वात उद्धतयोः मेघयोः गगने यथा
verses.iast:
sa samprahāraḥ tumulaḥ tayoḥ tasmin mahā mṛdhe |
babhūva vāta uddhatayoḥ meghayoḥ gagane yathā
verses.translation: As with two gigantic clouds up-heaved by the tornadic gusts will be hard hitting each other tempestuously in sky, the combat between those two, Ravana and Jataayu, became tempestuous in the sky.

glosses.meaning: in that, great [tempestuous,] combat [in sky, in forest]
by gust, ud dhatayoH = up, heaved

verses.devanagari:
तत् बभूव अद्भुतम् युद्धम् गृध्र राक्षसयोः तदा |
सपक्षयोः माल्यवतोः महा पर्वतयोः इव
verses.iast:
tat babhūva adbhutam yuddham gṛdhra rākṣasayoḥ tadā |
sapakṣayoḥ mālyavatoḥ mahā parvatayoḥ iva
verses.translation: As with a startling combat between two gigantic and winged mountains, called Mt. Maalyavanta-s, that combat between the eagle and demon then became a startling one.
notes: One commentator said that one Mt. Maalyavanta is in Dandaka forest and the other in Kishkindha, while another commentator said that one is in Dandaka forests and the other is nearby Mt. Meru. There appears to be no second Mt. Maalyavanta and the poet seems to be taking one mountain and mirroring it, and thus saying that if two selfsame mountains were to confront, then it will be disastrous. This is to narrate the equivalence between their courage and strength.

glosses.meaning: with, wings, between two Maalyavanta mountains

verses.devanagari:
ततो नालीक नाराचैः तीक्ष्ण अग्रैः च विकर्णिभिः |
अभ्यवर्षत् महाघोरैः गृध्र राजम् महाबलः
verses.iast:
tato nālīka nārācaiḥ tīkṣṇa agraiḥ ca vikar.hṇibhiḥ |
abhyavarṣat mahāghoraiḥ gṛdhra rājam mahābalaḥ
verses.translation: Then the great-mighty Ravana incessantly stormed the lord of eagles Jataayu, with arrows that have excruciating and highly dreadful arrowheads, like tubular arrows, iron arrows, and with arrows that have crescentic arrowheads.

glosses.meaning: with highly, dreadful naaliika naaraacaiH[sharaiH] = Naaliika [tubular,] Naaraaca [iron,] [with arrows]
upturned, ears [arrows with, crescentic arrowheads,] also

verses.devanagari:
स तानि शर जालानि गृध्रः पत्ररथ ईश्वरः |
जटायुः प्रतिजग्राह रावण अस्त्राणि संयुगे
verses.iast:
sa tāni śara jālāni gṛdhraḥ patraratha īśvaraḥ |
jaṭāyuḥ pratijagrāha rāvaṇa astrāṇi saṃyuge
verses.translation: That eagle Jataayu who is the lord of winged-chariots, namely birds, in turn sustained those arrays of Ravana's arrows in that combat.

verses.devanagari:
तस्य तीक्ष्ण नखाभ्याम् तु चरणाभ्याम् महाबलः |
चकार बहुधा गात्रे व्रणान् पतग सत्तमः
verses.iast:
tasya tīkṣṇa nakhābhyām tu caraṇābhyām mahābalaḥ |
cakāra bahudhā gātre vraṇān pataga sattamaḥ
verses.translation: But that great-mighty Jataayu severally made gashes on the body of Ravana with his two feet that have gashing claws for that bird is with best stamina.

glosses.meaning: which have gashing, claws, with two feet

verses.devanagari:
अथ क्रोधात् दशग्रीवः जग्राह दश मार्गणान् |
मृत्यु दण्ड निभान् घोरान् शत्रोर् निधन कान्क्षया
verses.iast:
atha krodhāt daśagrīvaḥ jagrāha daśa mārgaṇān |
mṛtyu daṇḍa nibhān ghorān śatror nidhana kānkṣayā
verses.translation: Now the Decahedral demon Ravana infuriately took up ten deadly arrows that are similar in their shine to the Shafts of the Terminator, wishful of the elimination of his enemy.

verses.devanagari:
स तैः बाणैः महावीर्यः पूर्ण मुक्तैः अजिह्म गैः |
बिभेद निशितैः तीक्ष्णैः गृध्रम् घोरैः शिली मुखैः
verses.iast:
sa taiḥ bāṇaiḥ mahāvīryaḥ pūrṇa muktaiḥ ajihma gaiḥ |
bibheda niśitaiḥ tīkṣṇaiḥ gṛdhram ghoraiḥ śilī mukhaiḥ
verses.translation: That highly energetic Ravana released and impaled the eagle with straight shooting arrows on fully stretching the bowstring up to his ear, whose steel-pointed arrowheads are sharp, hurtful, and deadly.

glosses.meaning: highly energetic one, he that Ravana

verses.devanagari:
स राक्षस रथे पश्यन् जानकीम् बाष्प लोचनाम् |
अचिंतयित्वा बाणाम् तान् राक्षसम् समभिद्रवत्
verses.iast:
sa rākṣasa rathe paśyan jānakīm bāṣpa locanām |
aciṃtayitvā bāṇām tān rākṣasam samabhidravat
verses.translation: That Jataayu on seeing teary-eyed Jaanaki in the chariot of the demon forcefully lunged towards that demon heedless of arrows that are lunging at him.

glosses.meaning: with teary, eyes, Jaanaki, while seeing

verses.devanagari:
ततो अस्य सशरम् चापम् मुक्ता मणि विभूषितम् |
चरणाभ्याम् महातेजा बभंज पतगोत्तमः
verses.iast:
tato asya saśaram cāpam muktā maṇi vibhūṣitam |
caraṇābhyām mahātejā babhaṃja patagottamaḥ
verses.translation: That unexcelled bird of high refulgence then shattered Ravana's bow which is decorated with pearls and gemstones, and on which an arrow is admitted targeting the eagle, just by the pair of his bare feet.

glosses.meaning: highly refulgent, among birds, unexcelled one
with, an arrow - admitted on bowstring

verses.devanagari:
ततो अन्यत् धनुः आदाय रावणः क्रोध मूर्च्छितः |
ववर्ष शर वर्षाणि शतशो अथ सहस्रशः
verses.iast:
tato anyat dhanuḥ ādāya rāvaṇaḥ krodha mūrcchitaḥ |
vavarṣa śara var.hṣāṇi śataśo atha sahasraśaḥ
verses.translation: Ravana convulsed in anger then took up another bow and stormed hundreds and thousands of arrow storms.

verses.devanagari:
शरैः आवारितः तस्य संयुगे पतगेश्वरः |
कुलायम् अभिसंप्राप्तः पक्षिः इव बभौ तदा
verses.iast:
śaraiḥ āvāritaḥ tasya saṃyuge patageśvaraḥ |
kulāyam abhisamprāptaḥ pakśiḥ iva babhau tadā
verses.translation: Nested in the arrows shot by Ravana that lordly bird Jataayu then shone forth in that combat like a bird that obtains a readymade nest.

glosses.meaning: covered with - engirded with, nested with

verses.devanagari:
स तानि शर जालानि पक्षाभ्याम् तु विधूय ह |
चरणाभ्याम् महातेजा बभंज अस्य महत् धनुः
verses.iast:
sa tāni śara jālāni pakśābhyām tu vidhūya ha |
caraṇābhyām mahātejā babhaṃja asya mahat dhanuḥ
verses.translation: On winnowing those arrays of arrows with both of his wings, he that highly refulgent Jataayu shattered the mighty bow of Ravana with both of his feet.

verses.devanagari:
तत् च अग्नि सदृशम् दीप्तम् रावणस्य शरावरम् |
पक्षाभ्याम् च महातेजा व्यधुनोत् पतगेश्वरः
verses.iast:
tat ca agni sadṛśam dīptam rāvaṇasya śarāvaram |
pakṣābhyām ca mahātejā vyadhunot patageśvaraḥ
verses.translation: That highly resplendent lord of birds also blasted off the armour of Ravana, which is glowing and flamelike in its flare, with both of his feet.
notes: The word used here for armour is śarāvaraand for this Pt. Satya Vrat says: 'Another word which is also not noticed by Monier Williams is śarāvara.It means an armour kavacaand occurs at least twice in the Ramayana...' i.e., here and at 3-64-49 of this canto.

glosses.meaning: = highly resplendent one, birds, lord of - Jataayu

verses.devanagari:
कांचन उरः छदान् दिव्यान् पिशाच वदनान् खरान् |
तान् च अस्य जव संपन्नान् जघान समरे बली
verses.iast:
kāṃcana uraḥ chadān divyān piśāca vadanān kharān |
tān ca asya java sampannān jaghāna samare balī
verses.translation: Mighty Jataayu also knocked off the ghost-faced mules yoked to the chariot of Ravana which are covered in golden armours and tantivy in fastness.

verses.devanagari:
अथ त्रिवेणु संपन्नम् कामगम् पावक अर्चिषम् |
मणि सोपान चित्र अंगम् बभंज च महारथम्
verses.iast:
atha triveṇu sampannam kāmagam pāvaka arciṣam |
maṇi sopāna citra aṃgam babhaṃja ca mahāratham
verses.translation: Then that great-chariot which is flourishing with three bamboos from chassis to yoke, and which traverses just by its steersman's wish, and which is crafted fantastically with gem-studded body and stairs, or, whose wheels are crafted with gold and gemstones, and which in its flare is like a Ritual-fire, Jataayu splintered down even that chariot of Ravana.

verses.devanagari:
पूर्ण चन्द्र प्रतीकाशम् छत्रम् च व्यजनैः सह |
पातयामास वेगेन ग्राहिभी राक्षसैः सह
verses.iast:
pūrṇa candra pratīkāśam chatram ca vyajanaiḥ saha |
pātayāmāsa vegena grāhibhī rākśasaiḥ saha
verses.translation: Jataayu swiftly collapsed the parasol of Ravana which in shine is mirroring the full moon, along with the regalia of white-royal-fur-fans, together with the demons handling them for fanning Ravana.

glosses.meaning: with handlers [of fans,] demons, along with

verses.devanagari:
सारथेः च अस्य वेगेन तुण्डेन च महत् शिरः |
पुनः व्यपाहरत् श्रीमान् पक्षिराजो महाबलः
verses.iast:
sāratheḥ ca asya vegena tuṇḍena ca mahat śiraḥ |
punaḥ vyapāharat śrīmān pakśirājo mahābalaḥ
verses.translation: Again that highly energetic and imposing king of birds pecked off the robust head of the charioteer of Ravana with beak.

glosses.meaning: with beak, took away - pecked off.

verses.devanagari:
स भग्न धन्वा विरथो हत अश्वो हत सारथिः |
अंकेन आदाय वैदेहीम् पपात भुवि रावणः
verses.iast:
sa bhagna dhanvā viratho hata aśvo hata sārathiḥ |
aṃkena ādāya vaidehīm papāta bhuvi rāvaṇaḥ
verses.translation: Now Ravana who is with his devastated bow, devoid of chariot, dispatched are his horses and departed is his charioteer, and such as he is, he on grabbing Vaidehi by her torso, or, placing her on the lower end of his torso, jumped to earth.
notes: Again the problem of 'untouchability of Seetha' occurred. Hence that compound ankena ādāya vaidehīm can be expressed in two ways, one is like the usual villain's grabbing by torso, and the other is like an ardent devotee of Goddess Lakshmi, keeping her on his torso. This is similar to the method adopted by Viraadha while handling Seetha.

glosses.meaning: Vaidehi, by her torso, grabbing, [or, taking her onto his torso]

verses.devanagari:
दृष्ट्वा निपतितम् भूमौ रावणम् भग्न वाहनम् |
साधु साधु इति भूतानि गृध्र राजम् अपूजयन्
verses.iast:
dṛṣṭvā nipatitam bhūmau rāvaṇam bhagna vāhanam |
sādhu sādhu iti bhūtāni gṛdhra rājam apūjayan
verses.translation: On seeing Ravana who is foundered onto earth from his crumbled vehicle, all beings like sylvan deities, caarana-s, siddha-s and suchlike, reverenced that lordly eagle Jataayu.

glosses.meaning: downwards, one who is foundered, at Ravana

verses.devanagari:
परिश्रान्तम् तु तम् दृष्ट्वा जरया पक्षि यूथपम् |
उत्पपात पुनर् हृष्टो मैथिलीम् गृह्य रावणः
verses.iast:
pariśrāntam tu tam dṛṣṭvā jarayā pakṣi yūthapam |
utpapāta punar hṛṣṭo maithilīm gṛhya rāvaṇaḥ
verses.translation: But on seeing the commandant of birds Jataayu is fatigued owing to his senescence, Ravana is gladdened and he again rose up to skies taking Maithili.

glosses.meaning: up, fallen - rose up to sky.

verses.devanagari:
तम् प्रहृष्टम् निधाय अंके रावणम् जनक आत्मजाम् |
गच्छंतम् खड्ग शेषम् च प्रणष्ट हत साधनम्
गृध्र राजः समुत्पत्य रावणम् समभिद्रवत् |
समावार्यम् महातेजा जटायुः इदम् अब्रवीत्
verses.iast:
tam prahṛṣṭam nidhāya aṃke rāvaṇam janaka ātmajām |
gacchaṃtam khaḍga śeṣam ca praṇaṣṭa hata sādhanam
gṛdhra rājaḥ samutpatya rāvaṇam samabhidravat |
samāvāryam mahātejā jaṭāyuḥ idam abravīt
verses.translation: The highly resplendent king of eagles Jataayu swiftly rose to sky dashing practically to forestall Ravana, which demon's assault devices are all demolished by now save for a single sword, but who is cheerful to spirit away the daughter of Janaka, and actually spiriting away holding her onto his flank, and Jataayu spoke this to such Ravana.

glosses.meaning: one who is cheerful - to Ravana
one having [single] sword, remnant [save for,] also
on flank, keeping [holding,] one who is going away

verses.devanagari:
वर्ज संस्पर्श बाणस्य भार्याम् रामस्य रावण |
अल्प बुद्धे हरसि एनाम् वधाय खलु रक्षसाम्
verses.iast:
varja saṃsparśa bāṇasya bhāryām rāmasya rāvaṇa |
alpa buddhe harasi enām vadhāya khalu rakṣasām
verses.translation: "You mean-minded Ravana, you abduct her whose husband wields arrows that touch off like the Thunderbolt of Indra, and this spite of yours is definitely for the destruction of all the demons.

glosses.meaning: Vajra, [Thunderbolt weapon of Indra,] with a touching off, one who has [wields] arrows
of all demons, for destruction, you abduct, definitely.

verses.devanagari:
स मित्र बन्धुः स अमात्यः स बलः स परिच्छदः |
विष पानम् पिबसि एतत् पिपासित इव उदकम्
verses.iast:
sa mitra bandhuḥ sa amātyaḥ sa balaḥ sa paricchadaḥ |
viṣa pānam pibasi etat pipāsita iva udakam
verses.translation: "As one thirsteth drinketh water, you drinketh venomous drink along with your friends, relatives, ministers, armies, and with your accomplices, as this abduction of Seetha itself is squirrelling away dangerous poison.

glosses.meaning: this [abduction of Seetha called consumption of venom]

verses.devanagari:
अनुबंधम् अजानंतः कर्मणाम् अविचक्षणाः |
शीघ्रम् एव विनश्यन्ति यथा त्वम् विनशिष्यसि
verses.iast:
anubaṃdham ajānaṃtaḥ karmaṇām avicakṣaṇāḥ |
śīghram eva vinaśyanti yathā tvam vinaśiṣyasi
verses.translation: "As with the mindless adventurers quickly getting ruination for they undertake self-ruinous exploits, unknowing the backlashes thereof, so also you too will ruin that quickly with this mindless adventure.

verses.devanagari:
बद्धः त्वम् काल पाशेन क्व गतः तस्य मोक्ष्यसे |
वधाय बडिशम् गृह्य स अमिषम् जलजो यथा
verses.iast:
baddhaḥ tvam kāla pāśena kva gataḥ tasya mokṣyase |
vadhāya baḍiśam gṛhya sa amiṣam jalajo yathā
verses.translation: "You are tethered for termination with the lasso of the Terminator, as with a fish that can go nowhere on its biting fishhook with a piece of flesh. How do you untether yourself from that lasso of the Terminator, even if you go anywhere?
notes: Vividly: The Terminator gives a sinner a longest rope possible to hang himself from a tallest tree. Perchance there may be fish that bites the bait, stripping fishhook from fish line, dives deep down to escape from the fisherman, and yet it cannot survive even there, because the fishhook is already in its throat, which the fish can neither vomit nor swallow. Thus, it is destined to die. Likewise, you bit the baited hook called Seetha and running away with that bait and hook around your neck, thereby the Terminator has already lassoed His noose around your neck, and perchance you may presently abscond from this hermitage, but not from that noose, called Rama's arrow, for a long time.

glosses.meaning: fish rod and line with fish-hook
wherever, you go, get released [whereby you untether yourself.]

verses.devanagari:
न हि जातु दुराधर्षौ काकुत्स्थौ तव रावण |
धर्षणम् च आश्रमस्य अस्य क्षमिष्येते तु राघवौ
verses.iast:
na hi jātu durādharṣau kākutsthau tava rāvaṇa |
dharṣaṇam ca āśramasya asya kṣamiṣyete tu rāghavau
verses.translation: "But, oh Ravana, the unassailable Raghava-s of Kakutstha dynasty will nevermore condone your assailing this hermitage.

glosses.meaning: those from Kakutstha dynasty, Raghava-s - Rama, Lakshmana

verses.devanagari:
यथा त्वया कृतम् कर्म भीरुणा लोक गर्हितम् |
तस्कर आचरितो मार्गो न एष वीर निषेवितः
verses.iast:
yathā tvayā kṛtam karma bhīruṇā loka garhitam |
taskara ācarito mār.hgo na eṣa vīra niṣevitaḥ
verses.translation: "Like a dastard you are committing a crime of thieving Seetha when none at home in the footsteps of thieves, this thieving is contemptible to society and condemnable by valiant ones.

glosses.meaning: by world [society,] contemptible, deed [crime,] being done [committed]
thieves, tramped, pathway [in the footsteps of thieves]
by valiant ones, adored by [acceptable, commendable by valiant ones]

verses.devanagari:
युध्यस्व यदि शूरो असि मुहूर्तम् तिष्ठ रावण |
शयिष्यसे हतो भूमौ यथा भ्राता खरः तथा
verses.iast:
yudhyasva yadi śūro asi muhūrtam tiṣṭha rāvaṇa |
śayiṣyase hato bhūmau yathā bhrātā kharaḥ tathā
verses.translation: "Stay for a moment, oh, Ravana, if you are valiant enough you can combat with Rama who will return right away, and at his hand you will be slain and sprawling on earth in the same way as Khara sprawled earlier.
notes: This verse is a repeat of verse at 3-50-23, and such iterations are not for want of paucity of verses or verbiage, but they are reckoned as the determination of the character to express his/her stance in similar terms.

glosses.meaning: slain, on earth, you will sprawl.

verses.devanagari:
परेत काले पुरुषो यत् कर्म प्रतिपद्यते |
विनाशाय आत्मनो अधर्म्यम् प्रतिपन्नो असि कर्म तत्
verses.iast:
pareta kāle puruṣo yat karma pratipadyate |
vināśāya ātmano adharmyam pratipanno asi karma tat
verses.translation: "A person undertakes such an unrighteous and fateful activity if only death looms large on him. You too have undertaken this unrighteous fateful activity only for your self-ruination.

verses.devanagari:
पाप अनुबंधो वै यस्य कर्मणः को नु तत् पुमान् |
कुर्वीत लोक अधिपतिः स्वयंभूः भगवान् अपि
verses.iast:
pāpa anubaṃdho vai yasya karmaṇaḥ ko nu tat pumān |
kur.hvīta loka adhipatiḥ svayambhūḥ bhagavān api
verses.translation: "If sin is consequential to any given activity who will undertake it? Even if that person vies with the Self-Born God and Lord of the Universe, namely Brahma, will he undertake it?" Thus Jataayu advised Ravana.

verses.devanagari:
एवम् उक्त्वा शुभम् वाक्यम् जटायुः तस्य रक्षसः |
निपपात भृशम् पृष्ठे दशग्रीवस्य वीर्यवान्
verses.iast:
evam uktvā śubham vākyam jaṭāyuḥ tasya rakṣasaḥ |
nipapāta bhṛśam pṛṣṭhe daśagrīvasya vīryavān
verses.translation: Even on speaking those commonsensical words to Ravana, Jataayu found him carrying off Seetha heedlessly, then that valorous Jataayu descended on the hind-side of that Decahedral demon Ravana, devastatingly.

glosses.meaning: this way, auspicious [commonsensical,] words, on speaking
demon, his, Decahedron's, on hind-side, on back

verses.devanagari:
तम् गृहीत्वा नखैः तीक्ष्णैः विददार समंततः |
अधिरूढो गज आरोहो यथा स्यात् दुष्ट वारणम्
verses.iast:
tam gṛhītvā nakhaiḥ tīkṣṇaiḥ vidadāra samaṃtataḥ |
adhirūḍho gaja āroho yathā syāt duṣṭa vāraṇam
verses.translation: On clasping Ravana with incisive claws Jataayu lacerated deeply and rampantly, as a mahout, an elephant-trainer-controller, sitting astride on it will try to control an uncontrollable elephant that is running amok with an incisive goad.

glosses.meaning: bad, elephant - an uncontrollable elephant that is running amok
as it will be -as he will try to control

verses.devanagari:
विददार नखैः अस्य तुण्डम् पृष्ठे समर्पयन् |
केशान् च उत्पाटयामास नख पक्ष मुख आयुधः
verses.iast:
vidadāra nakhaiḥ asya tuṇḍam pṛṣṭhe samarpayan |
keśān ca utpāṭayāmāsa nakha pakṣa mukha āyudhaḥ
verses.translation: Weaponed only with his claws, wings, and beak, Jataayu not only tore the back of Ravana asunder applying his beak and claws, but started to tweeze even his hair.

glosses.meaning: claws, wings, face [beak, only with] weaponed one

verses.devanagari:
स तथा गृध्र राजेन क्लिश्यमानो मुहुर् मुहुः |
अमर्ष स्फुरित ओष्ठः सन् प्राकंपत स राक्षसः
verses.iast:
sa tathā gṛdhra rājena kliśyamāno muhur muhuḥ |
amarṣa sphurita oṣṭhaḥ san prākampata sa rākṣasaḥ
verses.translation: His lips becoming intolerantly quivery when Ravana is exasperated by that king of eagles repetitiously, that demon staggered on to his right targeting the hovering eagle at his hind-side to fell it down.

glosses.meaning: by intolerance, quivering, lips, on becoming

verses.devanagari:
संपरिष्वज्य वैदेहीम् वामेन अंकेन रावणः |
तलेन अभिजघान आर्तो जटायुम् क्रोध मूर्चितः
verses.iast:
sampariṣvajya vaidehīm vāmena aṃkena rāvaṇaḥ |
talena abhijaghāna ārto jaṭāyum krodha mūrcitaḥ
verses.translation: Ravana who is aggrieved and convulsed in fury hit back Jataayu with his palm while firmly clutching Vaidehi onto his left flank.

verses.devanagari:
जटायुः तम् अतिक्रम्य तुण्डेन अस्य खग अधिपः |
वाम बाहून् दश तदा व्यपाहरत् अरिन्दमः
verses.iast:
jaṭāyuḥ tam atikramya tuṇḍena asya khaga adhipaḥ |
vāma bāhūn daśa tadā vyapāharat arindamaḥ
verses.translation: Jataayu, the lord of birds, being a vanquisher of enemies outstripped Ravana and ripped off ten left-arms of Ravana with his beak, with which left arms Ravana is clutching Vaidehi, in order to release her from his clutches.

verses.devanagari:
संच्छिन्न बाहोः सद्यो वै बाहवः सहसा अभवन् |
विष ज्वालावली युक्ता वल्मीकत् इव पन्नगाः
verses.iast:
sañcchinna bāhoḥ sadyo vai bāhavaḥ sahasā abhavan |
viṣa jvālāvalī yuktā valmīkat iva pannagāḥ
verses.translation: Though his arms are mutilated thus, they instantaneously ricocheted from his body like snakes possessing a series of venomous blazes sprawling out from a snake pit.

verses.devanagari:
ततः क्रोद्धात् दशग्रीवः सीताम् उत्सृज्य वीर्यवान् |
मुष्टिभ्याम् चरणाभ्याम् च गृध्र राजम् अपोथयत्
verses.iast:
tataḥ kroddhāt daśagrīvaḥ sītām utsṛjya vīryavān |
muṣṭibhyām caraṇābhyām ca gṛdhra rājam apothayat
verses.translation: The valorous Decahedron Ravana then threw off Seetha, and out of fury he scuffled with the king of eagles with fisticuffs and kicks, by both his feet and fists.

glosses.meaning: with both fists [fisticuffs,] with both feet [kicks]

verses.devanagari:
ततो मुहूर्तम् संग्रामो बभूव अतुल वीर्ययोः |
राक्षसानाम् च मुख्यस्य पक्षिणाम् प्रवरस्य च
verses.iast:
tato muhūrtam saṃgrāmo babhūva atula vīryayoḥ |
rākṣasānām ca mukhyasya pakṣiṇām pravarasya ca
verses.translation: Then there chanced an encounter for some time between those two valorous ones with mutually outweighing capabilities, namely the chieftain of demons and the chief of the birds.

verses.devanagari:
तस्य व्यायच्छमानस्य रामस्य अर्थे अथ रावणः |
पक्षौ पादौ च पार्श्वौ च खड्गम् उद्धृत्य सो अच्छिनत्
verses.iast:
tasya vyāyacchamānasya rāmasya arthe atha rāvaṇaḥ |
pakṣau pādau ca pārśvau ca khaḍgam uddhṛtya so acchinat
verses.translation: Ravana brandishing his sword at Jataayu, who is revolting for the sake of Rama, hewed off both of his wings, sides, and feet.

glosses.meaning: one who is up raising - revolting

verses.devanagari:
स छिन्न पक्षः सहसा रक्षसा रौद्र कर्मणा |
निपपात महा गृध्रो धरण्याम् अल्प जीवितः
verses.iast:
sa chinna pakṣaḥ sahasā rakṣasā raudra karmaṇā |
nipapāta mahā gṛdhro dharaṇyām alpa jīvitaḥ
verses.translation: When that demon of cruel actions has ruptured his wings that colossal eagle Jataayu immediately fell down to earth with a lessened life.

verses.label: 3.51.43b
verses.devanagari:
ततः तु तम् पत्ररथम् मही तले
निपातितम् रावण वेग मर्दितम् |
पुनः च संगृह्य शशि प्रभ आनना
रुरोद सीता जनक आत्मजा तदा
verses.iast:
tataḥ tu tam patraratham mahī tale
nipātitam rāvaṇa vega marditam |
punaḥ ca saṅgṛhya śaśi prabha ānanā
ruroda sītā janaka ātmajā tadā
verses.translation: But then Seetha, the daughter of Janaka, whose face vies with moonshine hugged eagle Jataayu, whom Ravana has subjugated with his forcefulness and felled down onto the surface of earth, and she wept over incessantly.
notes: Seetha is hugging Jataayu. 'Is it admissible or not...' is another debatable issue. 'Because it is bird, it may be handled...' is one adjustment, while the other is, 'when Jataayu is a personified entity and a friend of Dasharatha, this bird is as good as a man. So, Seetha's touching him shall be a taboo...' The commentators deal this aspect in the next chapter of this canto.

glosses.meaning: again [further, incessantly,] taken in hands [hugged,] wept over.

verses.devanagari:
तम् दृष्ट्वा पतितम् भूमौ क्षतज आर्द्रम् जटायुषम् |
अभ्यधावत वैदेही स्व बंधुम् इव दुःखिता
verses.iast:
tam dṛṣṭvā patitam bhūmau kṣataja ārdram jaṭāyuṣam |
abhyadhāvata vaidehī sva baṃdhum iva duḥkhitā
verses.translation: On seeing Jataayu fallen on earth and dampened with blood Vaidehi fell into a fit of weeping and ran towards him as if he is her own relative.

glosses.meaning: fell into a fit of weeping

verses.devanagari:
तम् नील जीमूत निकाश कल्पम्
सुपाण्डुर उरस्कम् उदार वीर्यम् |
ददर्श लंका अधिपतिः पृथिव्याम्
जटायुषम् शान्तम् इव अग्नि दावम्
verses.iast:
tam nīla jīmūta nikāśa kalpam
supāṇḍura uraskam udāra vīryam |
dadarśa laṃkā adhipatiḥ pṛthivyām
jaṭāyuṣam śāntam iva agni dāvam
verses.translation: Ravana, the monarch of Lanka, gazed at that worthily valorous Jataayu, who in his shine is like a blue-black cloud with a whitely white chest and who by now is like a quiescent fire-storm flattened onto ground.
notes: The cloudy blackness is simile to the black feathers of the eagle, and to the charred material by a wildfire. The whitely white colour is to the whitish feathers on the chest of the eagle, and to the white ashes overlaid on the charred material by wildfire, before they ashen. Thus, Jataayu fell down in a supine posture.
